mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.0% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in accommodative monetary policy without requiring additional trigger conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.0%, or Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point increase in unemployment rate over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate increases (>0.25pp in 1 month) and unemployment rates below 4.0% signal aggressive monetary tightening amid tight labor markets, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through heightened recession fears.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in 1 month AND UNRATE < 4.0%
regime_hint: monetary tightening with tight labor market
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During recessions (GDPC1 annualized growth < 0.5%), a 1.0% monthly rebound in housing starts (HOUST) signals leading sector recovery, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic expansion expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 0.5% annualized AND HOUST rises > 1.0% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly nonfarm payrolls growth exceeding 100,000 jobs consistently signals robust corporate hiring and consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring regime-specific conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS > 100k, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Core inflation exceeding 3.5% annualized (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation, prompting aggressive monetary policy that depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous industrial production decline (>0.5% in 1 month) and housing starts increase (>0.5% in 1 month) signal stagflationary risks from manufacturing supply shocks amid strong housing demand, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 1 month AND HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During economic expansions (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0%), a 0.8% monthly increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as earnings growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized AND RSAFS rises > 0.8% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows remains below 0.02.
